findings.title: V2 client permission methods throw instead of degrading
findings.body: ClientPermissionsV2 is installed for every realm whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on (MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()), but isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource, and the Policy accessors all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Those methods are still called by the admin client management-permissions API, so opening or updating a client's permissions tab returns 500 for every realm, not only realms using FGAP. canExchangeTo (line 148) throws the same way, so token-exchange permission checks 500 instead of denying. setPermissionsEnabled must no-op or return a normal error, and the boolean/read methods must return false/empty when V2 does not use per-client authz resources.

findings.title: Schema init does not add Clients type to existing realms
findings.body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. That client was created by the earlier Users-only schema, so upgraded realms never get the Clients resource, or the new configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Creating or evaluating a Clients permission then fails with missing-scope or missing-resource errors, and ClientPermissionsV2 falls through to a null type resource. Init needs to add any schema resource types and scopes that are not already present.

findings.title: Role-mapping checks ignore manage-clients and manage
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission for that scope. Unlike canManage in the same class, they do not treat AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS as allowed, and they do not treat a Clients manage grant as allowed. A realm admin (or any caller who can manage the client) is therefore forbidden from mapping client roles, composite roles, or client-scope roles unless a separate FGAP map-roles policy exists. V1 granted these via the manage-clients short-circuit inside permission checks.

findings.title: Per-client evaluation skips all-clients policies and can NPE
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads only the per-client resource when one exists and never evaluates the Clients type resource in that case. FGAP requires both: a positive all-clients grant must still apply when the client already has a resource for another scope, and a negative all-clients policy must still deny a positive per-client grant. As written, all-clients manage/view is ignored whenever any per-client resource exists (incorrect deny), and a negative all-clients policy does not override a positive per-client policy (incorrect allow). If the per-client resource is missing and getResourceTypeResource returns null (schema not migrated, or admin permissions not enabled for this server), findByResource(server, null) on line 219 throws NullPointerException and the admin call 500s instead of returning false.

findings.title: Per-client resources are created without a type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates the client resource by name and scopes but never setType(CLIENTS). The aggregate Clients resource created in init() does set its type. ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission then uses resourceStore.findByType(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), so it will not see per-client grants. It will see the aggregate resource and add its name "Clients" to the granted id set, which is not a client id. Callers that filter the client list or role-mapping targets with this set therefore omit clients the user was granted and never match a real client id.

findings.title: Client resource names are not resolved for display
findings.body: getResourceName resolves Users resources to a username (or "All users") but has no Clients branch. Per-client resources are stored under the internal client id and display name is never set, so permission listings fall through to resource.getDisplayName() and show null instead of the clientId. After a client is deleted the orphaned resource still will not be reported as missing, unlike the user path which throws ModelIllegalStateException.

findings.title: Client-removal cleanup throws or skips V2 resources
findings.body: The removal listener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, but management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. If both features are on, ClientRemovedEvent calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws UnsupportedOperationException and can fail client deletion. If only V2 is on, the listener is skipped entirely. Nothing deletes the FGAP resource that getOrCreateResource stored under the client id on the admin-permissions client, so deleted clients leave orphaned resources and policies.

findings.title: Configure test rotates the shared admin client secret
findings.body: testConfigureOnlyOneClient calls generateNewSecret() on myclient, which is the confidential client used by the injected realmAdminClient (and by other tests that log in with client secret mysecret). onAfter only deletes scope permissions and does not restore the secret, name, or default client scopes mutated by these tests. Later tests in the same realm then fail authentication or see a changed client, depending on method order. The new map-roles-client-scope scope is also never exercised.

findings.title: requireView javadoc describes the wrong contract
findings.body: requireView is documented as returning true when canView() is true, and requireViewClientScopes (line 101) as returning true when canViewClientScopes() is true. Both methods are void and are specified elsewhere to throw ForbiddenException. Callers reading only these comments will treat them as predicates.
